_comment: Connector-specific edits a cli-printing-press reprint or onboard --resume must NOT clobber. check_handfixes.py asserts every marker below is still present (and banned anti-patterns absent) and FAILS CI if a reprint dropped one. This connector was minted from a HAND-AUTHORED spec (no public OpenAPI); see project_connectwise_control_needs_creds_block.

handfixes.summary: manifest.json name/entry_point/command use the clean `connectwise-control-mcp`, not the press `-pp-mcp`
handfixes.why: onboard re-copies the SOURCE manifest each --resume; the press source keeps `-pp-mcp`. The repo ships `connectwise-control-mcp`. See project_onboard_manifest_deleak_and_envvar.

handfixes.summary: manifest.json carries a real product description, not the verbose authored-spec info.description ('Unofficial OpenAPI 3 description ...')
handfixes.why: The hand-authored OpenAPI's info.description (a long unofficial/wire-format note) propagated to the README hero + plugin/marketplace/server.json. Authored a real one-liner in the SOURCE manifest. A fresh mint re-emits the spec description.

handfixes.summary: Per-instance CONNECTWISE_CONTROL_BASE_URL is required in manifest + server.json; BASE_URL and USERNAME are non-secret, PASSWORD secret (HTTP Basic)
handfixes.why: ScreenConnect is appliance/instance-hosted - config.go reads CONNECTWISE_CONTROL_BASE_URL but the press manifest shipped only USERNAME+PASSWORD (the per-instance BASE_URL-omission pattern). Auth is HTTP Basic (USERNAME + PASSWORD); a URL and a username are not secrets, so server.json must mark BASE_URL + USERNAME isSecret:false. A fresh mint drops BASE_URL and marks all three secret. See project_veeam_onboard_traps.

handfixes.summary: Governance has a 'Session and host control' human-in-the-loop tier; gen_governance DROPPED sessions run-command (remote code execution on a guest)
handfixes.why: `sessions run-command` runs an arbitrary command on a customer's guest machine (RCE) - the single highest-risk command - and gen_governance left it out of the tier table entirely (the 'command'-named-write blind spot, same class as connectwise-automate's command-execute). Hand-added a Session-and-host-control tier covering run-command + add-event-to, an Access-grant tier (get-access-token), and Admin (save-user/delete-user). A full reprint re-runs the classifier and reverts. See project_connectwise_automate_onboard_traps + feedback_secret_read_commands_not_read_tier.

handfixes.summary: SKILL.md Auth Setup documents HTTP Basic with all three env vars (BASE_URL + USERNAME + PASSWORD), not the generic single-token `auth set-token` model
handfixes.why: The press generated a generic 'auth setup -> get a key -> set USERNAME=<your-key>' section that omitted PASSWORD + BASE_URL and implied a single token - a user following only it cannot authenticate (HTTP Basic needs username+password+host). Adversarial review caught it (P1). A re-vendor re-emits the generic single-token section.

handfixes.summary: page.json command examples use the stripped `connectwise-control-cli`, never `connectwise-control-pp-cli`
handfixes.why: check_cli_claims is blind to the binary-name prefix, so a `-pp-cli` example would pass the gate but fail for users and ship into the published docs page + llms. See project_veeam_onboard_traps.

handfixes.summary: SKILL.md + guide.md stay free of Printing Press / npx / go-install / openclaw-install-block leaks and the verbose .ashx spec-description intro
handfixes.why: onboard only de-leaks the SKILL.md description. The body H1/prereqs/MCP-install, the openclaw frontmatter `install:` block (printing-press-library go module), guide.md's install section, and the raw authored-spec info.description (with .ashx/christaylorcodes wire-format jargon) all survive a re-vendor. See project_onboard_skillmd_guide_deleak.

handfixes.summary: delete-user / add-event-to / get-info carry NO `create` Cobra alias; the press auto-aliases the alphabetically-first POST command in each resource group to `create`
handfixes.why: The press assigns `Aliases: []string{"create"}` to the first POST command per resource group. Here that lands on `security delete-user` (so `security create` would DELETE an instance user), `sessions add-event-to` (queues control events like Wake-on-LAN), and `audit get-info` - none of which create anything; the delete-user case is a catastrophic footgun. check_cli_claims is blind to Cobra aliases (project_onboard_cobra_alias_cli_claims_blindspot) so the gate passed; CodeRabbit flagged it on PR #99. A reprint re-adds the alias - remove it from all three command files. Systemic press bug; a retro should teach the press not to alias destructive/non-create POSTs to `create`.

handfixes.summary: doctor probes a real GET endpoint with the real credential and refuses to dial a placeholder base_url, instead of calling any HTTP response 'reachable' and never checking the credential
handfixes.why: `doctor` is the command every SKILL, guide and docs page tells an operator to run to confirm the connector works, and it could not tell a working install from a broken one. It called any HTTP response to `GET /` "reachable" and rendered it green, so a base_url aimed at the vendor's web UI (where every API path 404s) and a token rejected with 401 on every call both produced an all-green report. On this connector family it also never probed the credential at all: it printed "present, not verified" and left the operator to guess. The mirror defect: a connector whose shipped base_url default is a placeholder dialled the placeholder host, and the DNS failure rendered as "FAIL API: unreachable" - telling a correctly-credentialled operator they were broken without naming the one variable that would fix it. Several placeholder hosts resolve through live wildcard DNS and answer real HTTP, so dialling one produced a confident green verdict against a stranger's server. Measured and gated by tools/maintainer/check_doctor_truth.py. See issue #282.

handfixes.summary: every operator credential this connector reads is declared on all three install channels: manifest.json (.mcpb), server.json (MCP Registry) and mcp-install.md (manual install)
handfixes.why: Issue #282 ('three live-verified connectors prompt for the wrong credentials'). A connector is installed through THREE independent channels that each carry their own copy of the credential list: manifest.json server.mcp_config.env (what the .mcpb bundle hands Claude Desktop, which has no shell profile, no config.toml and no export - so an undeclared variable is a variable nobody is ever asked for), server.json environmentVariables (the MCP Registry publish channel), and mcp-install.md's copy-paste JSON blocks plus its remote launch line (the manual path, which never touches the bundle at all). The fleet-wide audit found 60 of 65 connectors under-declaring 122 operator-facing variables in the manifest, 61 of 65 mcp-install.md pages omitting 125, and hudu's server.json missing the base URL its manifest marks required. connectwise-control was already correct on all three channels; the ledger entry exists so a re-onboard cannot make it wrong. manifest.json, server.json and mcp-install.md are ALL regenerated by /msp-skills-publish on an UPDATE or re-onboard, so without this ledger a regeneration silently drops every declaration and CI stays green (check_env_schema.py is wired --warn). The asserts below name the specific credentials, not a count, so dropping one and adding another cannot cancel out. The 4.34.2 reprint adds the operator switches CONNECTWISE_CONTROL_MCP_READ_ONLY, CONNECTWISE_CONTROL_NO_LOCAL_DATA and CONNECTWISE_CONTROL_MCP_HTTP_TOKEN, plus the CONNECTWISE_CONTROL_USER_AGENT override, on all three channels; server.json marks the user name secret to match the manifest.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: cli-printing-press should emit server.mcp_config.env, the matching user_config prompts, server.json environmentVariables and mcp-install.md's env blocks from ONE declaration of the connector's operator-facing environment, so the three channels cannot be generated out of step. Until then check_env_schema.py compares all three and this ledger pins them.

handfixes.summary: export --output closes its (kit-routed) output file on every return, including an API error: the open no longer shadows RunE's named err
handfixes.why: The generated `f, err := openExportOutput(...)` inside the --output block declared a new err, so the deferred close tested that inner (nil) err and never ran when the export returned an API error. With the output chokepoint the file is a filter pipe, and the unclosed pipe kept the process from exiting: `export clients --output f.jsonl` after a 401 hung (TestExportOutputReturnsAfterAnAPIError, seen failing 3 of 4 runs). Fleet note: every connector that took the ported chokepoint edit on export.go carries the same shadowing. handfixes.summary: The HTTP Basic credential and every API request go only to the scheme, host and port of the configured instance (CONNECTWISE_CONTROL_BASE_URL); every redirect hop must stay on that origin, a non-ASCII host never matches, and an unparseable base URL pins nothing (every request refused). Installed on every CLI, novel and MCP client by registerClientHook (internal/cli/cwc_guard.go), with the response cache off and --dry-run clients refusing every send. The credential kit's outbound guard (credkit-wiring) wraps this pin on every send.
handfixes.why: Credential rule host pinning: the generated client sends the ApiIntegrationCode header to whatever URL it is handed and its CheckRedirect strips only the named auth headers, so a Location to another host or an absolute path from an MCP argument would carry the key off the vendor API. One origin, taken from the configured base URL; an operator who sets CONNECTWISE_CONTROL_BASE_URL moves the pin with it. Ported to connectwise-control from the atera 4.34.2 reprint (one credential layer across the fleet). Ported to connectwise-control from the autotask 4.34.2 reprint (one credential layer across the fleet).

handfixes.summary: The shared credential kit (tools/maintainer/credkit, vendored at cli/internal/credkit) is wired by hand and replaces this connector's own credential layer. internal/credwire/declarations.go holds the one Declarations literal (HTTP Basic user name and password, the MCP HTTP bearer sent nowhere, the access grant's accessToken and join url as response fields, the auth set-credentials positionals, --deliver webhooks and the run profile stores held at startup); each main starts with credkit.Start and ends with credkit.Exit; every client, feedback, webhook and probe request goes through credkit.Transport (client.OutboundGuard around the origin pin); every file write except the 0600 credential store and the config file goes through the kit (cliutil.AtomicWriteCredentialFile is that declared exemption); stdout and stderr are the kit's pipes; a config or credentials file read after startup is held before it is parsed (cliutil.HoldConfigFile).

handfixes.summary: No request, and so no HTTP Basic credential, is sent while the base URL is empty or the shipped placeholder https://your-instance.screenconnect.com, whatever supplied it (built-in default, config file, --config, CONNECTWISE_CONTROL_BASE_URL, the MCP server's environment) and in any spelling (case, trailing dot, port, userinfo, path, scheme). client.doInternal refuses before it builds a request and the origin pin refuses at the transport, with a configuration error (exit 10) naming CONNECTWISE_CONTROL_BASE_URL and base_url. The placeholder is never persisted (config.toml base_url, credentials.toml server), is no trusted origin for stored credentials, is not the kit's built-in base_url origin (Declarations.BaseURL.Default is a template), and is not pre-filled by the .mcpb form, server.json or the guide's manual JSON block. doctor reports every spelling as not configured.
handfixes.why: Adversarial review 2026-11-05 (P1, .review/adversarial-2026-11-05.json): with no base URL configured, every data command (generated endpoints, the sessions stale and security access-review novels) in the CLI and over MCP sent the operator's Basic user name and password to https://your-instance.screenconnect.com, a live host on ConnectWise's public cloud domain whose instance name a stranger can own. Only doctor treated it as a placeholder. auth set-credentials (the command's own --help example) wrote it into config.toml as base_url and into credentials.toml as the credential's server; the .mcpb install form and server.json pre-filled the required base URL with it; credwire.Declarations named it as the kit's base_url origin, so the kit's outbound guard allowed it. The generated config.go keeps the placeholder as Load's default (the press emits it from the spec's server URL, and check_doctor_truth.py reads it to run its placeholder state), so the refusal lives at the one chokepoint every request passes. Tests seen failing then passing (.review/seen/placeholder-host-seen-failing.log, placeholder-host-seen-passing.log): TestPlaceholderBaseURLRefusedBeforeTheTransport, TestPlaceholderBaseURLRefusedFromEverySource, TestPlaceholderCommandsSendNothing, TestDoctorReportsEverySpellingOfThePlaceholder, TestSaveCredentialsNeverPersistsThePlaceholder, TestBuiltinPlaceholderIsNoTrustedCredentialOrigin, TestDeclarationsNameNoPlaceholderOrigin, and the built-binary TestPlaceholderHostCLISendsNothing and TestPlaceholderHostMCPSendsNothing (HTTPS_PROXY at a loopback recorder; before the fix it logged CONNECT your-instance.screenconnect.com:443 for every command and MCP tool).
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: cli-printing-press should not emit a resolvable placeholder host as a connector's default base URL: an instance-hosted API's spec server should be a template (https://{instance}.screenconnect.com), which the generated client, the doctor and the kit already treat as not configured.

handfixes.summary: a row the credential kit withholds from the store is skipped and named; the rest of the batch is stored, sync keeps walking, and the run still succeeds, naming the row ids on stderr and in its summary
handfixes.why: One withheld row aborted the whole batch transaction, and sync returned on it, so a single large ordinary record (or one that really carried a held credential) stopped the resource and every row after it was never synced (#612, hubspot-calls-crm). The row is still withheld; it is now named, and the watermark stays so the next run fetches it again. Re-applied after a reprint by replay_handfixes.py (recipe withheld-rows). synccpu (2026-11-09): a withheld row no longer fails the resource. mcp2 measured hubspot-calls-crm row 80663490159 turning the whole sync into exit 1, so the server never marked the connector synced. Now the resource ends stored with the ids named (stderr warning, a sync_warning rows_withheld event per page, and "withheld" in the summary), the run exits 0 when every other row stored, and the resource's checkpoint stays where the attempt began so the next run fetches the row again.

handfixes.summary: sync wraps the event writer its parallel workers share in syncSerialWriter (internal/cli/sync_event_writer.go), so two workers never call Write on it at once.
handfixes.why: The generated sync hands cmd.OutOrStdout() (or ErrOrStderr() in machine output) to every --concurrency worker, and each writes sync_start, progress and error events. os.Stdout tolerates that; the writers --deliver (a mirror into a bytes.Buffer) and --receipt-file / --audit-dir (a running SHA-256) install do not, nor does an in-process caller's buffer: Windows CI on PR #655 panicked in bytes.Buffer.grow from syncResource, and go test -race found 28 races on veeam. TestSyncWorkerPoolSerializesEventWrites pins it. A reprint regenerates sync.go and drops the wrap; tools/maintainer/replay_handfixes.py re-applies it (fleet_handfixes.json sync-event-writer-serialized).
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side (mvanhorn/cli-printing-press#5369): the sync template should serialize the event writer its top-level worker pool shares, as its dependent path already does with lockedWriter.

handfixes.summary: the adaptive limiter's blind ramp raises only a rate the last Wait slept on, so sync's rate_rps reports a real pace
handfixes.why: On a header-less API the ramp multiplied the rate by 1.25 every 10 successes with no ceiling: mcp2's hubspot sync printed rate_rps 6.6e24 (about 2,500 requests), and after such a ramp a 429's halving could no longer slow a single request. A rate the requests never reach is no longer raised. Re-applied after a reprint by replay_handfixes.py (recipe limiter-paced).

retired.reason: tools/maintainer/fleet_handfixes.json: Press 4.34.0 builds a per-command blocked set (blockedDestinationFlags, blockedInputFlags, root control-plane flags), removes those flags from each tool's schema, refuses any undeclared argument name (so "db=/path" is refused) and skips '=' names in cliArgsFromMCP.

tools/maintainer/fleet_handfixes.json: Upstreamed as cli-printing-press #4647: every value-carrying branch of cliArgsFromMCP joins the value to its flag (--k=v, one element per list item), and the press generates TestCliArgsFromMCP_ValueCannotSmuggleBlockedFlag.

tools/maintainer/fleet_handfixes.json: The note paused HTTP mode until a reprint because the build served HTTP with no token. Press 4.34.0 HTTP mode refuses to start without <PREFIX>_MCP_HTTP_TOKEN, answers 401 without the right bearer, binds 127.0.0.1 by default and refuses a non-loopback address without TLS; onboard.py now writes HTTP guidance that follows the binary (cc-skills #14) and never writes this note, so the entry would fail on every re-onboard.

tools/maintainer/fleet_handfixes.json: Press 4.34.0's cobratree mirror derives one blocked set per command (destination, input, mcp:write-flags, mcp:read-flags and root control-plane flags), leaves those flags out of the tool schema and refuses them, and any undeclared argument, by name.
